chunks: ‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Mūsā ibn Bābawayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from al-Ḥasan ibn ‘Ali al-Washā, who said:

I asked Imam al-Riḍā (peace be upon him) about the Ziyārah of the grave of Abi al-Ḥasan (peace be upon him): is it like the Ziyārah of the grave of al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him)? He replied, 'Yes.' And Muḥammad ibn Ya‘qūb narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, through his chain, the same.
ai.seo_question: Is the reward for visiting Imam Kazim's grave equal to Imam Hussain's?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Imam al-Rida (a.s.), elevates the status of Imam Musa al-Kazim’s grave in Baghdad to match that of Imam al-Husayn’s shrine in Karbala, highlighting the continuity of spiritual merit across the Ahl al-Bayt. The dual narration in Kamil al-Ziyarat underscores the reliability of this equivalence, reflecting the Shia scholarly view that the sanctity of the Imams’ resting places is intrinsically linked to their divine station rather than the location of their martyrdom.
